newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall on Fed chief's latest market warning.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall on Fed chief's latest market warning.

text.p: Stocks fell Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warned that investors might have boosted the market too high and hinted at an interest rate hike in coming months.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 55.03 points at 6,983.18, although it rebounded from a loss of more than 120 points. In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,791 to 750 on active volume of 566 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Greenspan, delivering his semi-annual report on the economy to the Senate, spoke in surprisingly blunt terms of his concerns about the risks of inflation as well as the dramatic increase in stock prices.
The market's slide came one day after the blue-chip Dow index came within 30 points of its Feb. 18 record closing high of 7,067.46, which was its 13th milestone so far this year.

The Fed chief, whose passing rhetorical reference to "irrational exuberance" in a December speech sent financial markets reeling, left little question he remained concerned about the market's advance and urged caution.
"Such caution seems especially warranted with regard to the sharp rise in equity prices during the last two years," Greenspan said. "These gains have obviously raised questions of sustainability."
He also said inflation remains "quiescent" but warned the Fed might have to raise interest rates in anticipation of inflation.

The comments sent a jolt through the bond market, triggering selling that pushed the 30-year Treasury bond 1-17/32 lower, which sent its yield jumping to 6.78 percent from Tuesday's close of 6.66 percent.
Despite the stock market's partial rebound, analysts said Greenspan appeared to accomplish his goal of talking down the market.
"It looks like Greenspan did a better job of jawboning the market this time," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
"I think he's got the bond market clearly thinking the Fed's going to raise rates instead of doing nothing and that's taken the steam out of this market," he said.
With many analysts already warning the stock market was due for a pause, several said any further advances were almost certainly on hold for now.
"I do think his remarks may, on top of the strong performance we've seen this year, serve to be something of a constraint on the upside," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.
The interest rate sensitive financial and transportation sectors were hit especially hard as a result of the bond market's decline.
Among financials, BankAmerica Corp. fell 2-1/2 to 119-3/8, Merrill Lynch & Co. fell 2-1/8 to 95-3/4 and Chase Manhattan Corp. sank 2-1/2 to 103-1/4.
Southwest Airlines Co. slipped 7/8 to 23-7/8 and United Airlines parent company UAL Corp. fell 1-3/8 to 59-1/8.
Elsewhere, McDonald's Corp. dropped 2-5/8 to 44-5/8. The company confirmed it was considering chain-wide reductions in the prices of various sandwiches.

Fears that the discounting could trigger a price war also cut into shares of fast-food franchise competitors like Wendy's International Inc., which fell 1-1/2 to 20-3/4. Burger King's parent, Grand Metropolitan Plc shed one point to 30-5/8.
Petrolite Corp. jumped 10-3/8 to 58-3/8 after agreeing to be acquired by Baker Hughes Corp.
Shares in Baker Hughes, which will pay $61 in stock for each Petrolite share, ended unchanged at 35-1/2.

Dell Computer Corp. rose 3-5/8 to 75-3/4 in the first trading after the company reported stronger than expected earnings. Other direct marketing personal computer companies were also strong, including Gateway 2000 Inc., which gained 3-3/8 to 64-5/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 7.14 points to 1,340.55.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 6.35 to 805.68. The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.68 to 597.31.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 3.39 to 422.14. The average share was down 35 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,692.255, down 55.304 or 0.71 percent.
